About / Our Mission Declaration Pledge Lexicon Early Adopters How It Works Installation FAQs Contact & Support Counsel Handoff Events Noted Counsel Policies & Procedures Terms of Service Privacy Notice POPS NOTED COUNSEL Noted Counsel This page explains the POPS merit-recognition program for counsel. It is informational and is not a referral marketplace. No Rank. No Referral. Only Merit. POPS Noted Counsel is a positive-only merit-recognition page for attorneys who made a meaningful positive impression on a POPS user. Recognition may reflect professionalism, honesty, preparation, respectful treatment, clear communication, or meaningful service to a parent trying to stay present and organized for their child. What This Is POPS Noted Counsel exists to preserve and share carefully moderated positive recognition from real POPS users who had a direct, first-hand experience with an attorney. It is meant to recognize merit—not popularity, advertising budget, status, or influence. What This Is Not Not an attorney ranking system Not a star-rating or score-based review page Not a paid attorney directory Not a referral service or lead-generation program Not a “best attorney” list Not a public complaint board Not a guarantee that an attorney will accept a case or achieve a result Recognition Rules Only POPS Noted Users may submit a Merit Recognition. Attorneys cannot nominate themselves. Attorneys cannot buy recognition, placement, or visibility. There are no stars, scores, ranks, tiers, or “top attorney” labels. POPS does not publish negative reviews, attacks, or public disputes. Recognition must come from a real, first-hand positive experience. Private case information, child information, and outcome claims are not published. What Merit Can Look Like A POPS user may recognize an attorney for treating them with dignity, clearly explaining options, being honest about costs and limits, reviewing organized materials carefully, using a POPS timeline or packet effectively, or helping a parent understand what mattered next. A Noted Counsel recognition does not claim that an attorney is superior to another attorney. It does not promise a legal result, availability, affordability, or case acceptance. Why POPS Built This POPS helps fathers and parents arrive more prepared—with clearer timelines, preserved records, factual notes, and organized materials for professional review. When a POPS user is genuinely helped by an attorney who shows merit, that attorney may be recognized here with dignity and without turning the process into advertising, rankings, or referral money. Noted by users. Never bought. Never ranked. Recognized only for merit. Back to Landing Get POPS Windows Android Beta program Early adopters Installation FAQs Contact & privacy support P.O.P.S. Declaration First Order of Protection and Service Mission Statement POPS - the Proof of Presence System - exists to restore men to their God-given appointment as the First Order of Protection in the home. It equips fathers with the discipline, record-keeping, and truth-preserving tools needed to stand watch over their families, remain accountable in conflict, and protect what has been entrusted to them. POPS strengthens the man, safeguards the record, and preserves the truth when presence is questioned, challenged, or denied. POPS is not a support group. It is a support machine - built to keep a man aligned, sober-minded, and anchored to his calling, even in the hardest seasons of fatherhood. About This Declaration The P.O.P.S. Declaration is the foundational document of the First Order of Protection. It is not a policy, a slogan, or a motivational speech. It is the formal articulation of what men have always been in the home: the first responder, the first defender, the first witness, and the first line of protection long before institutions existed. This Declaration defines the charge, the duty, and the office of the father - not as a cultural role, but as a God-given appointment. It affirms the rights, responsibilities, and presence of the man who stands between his family and the dark, and calls that role by its true name: P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System. Preamble When in the course of a family's life, danger does not announce itself, when the call for help cannot wait for sirens, when the wolf is at the door and the door is the only thing between the wolf and the children, there must stand, in that gap, a man. Not a badge. Not a uniform. A father. Before there were Courts of Protection Services, before there were County Officers of Public Safety, before any institution wore the name of guardian, there was the man of the house, standing watch, armed with nothing but resolve and the authority given to him by his Creator. We call this what it has always been: P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System. The First Order of Protection and Service. This is not a replacement for law. This is the foundation law was built upon. When the C.O.P.S. cannot get there in time, and there will be moments they cannot, the P.O.P.S. is already there. He was never not there. That is the whole of the charge. We hold these truths to be self-evident, God-given, and undeniable: that every father is entrusted with rights, privileges, and responsibilities that no government granted and no government may revoke; that presence is not passive but is itself a duty; and that a man who stands watch over his household stands in an office older than nations. The Articles Article I On the Origin of the Charge The duty of a man to protect his household is not granted by any government, council, or institution of man. It precedes them all. It was given at the founding of the family itself, and it answers to a higher authority than any badge or statute. What the State formalizes as protective services, the home has always practiced as the first and oldest service of all. Article II On the Nature of Presence Protection is not an event. It is a condition. A man does not become a protector in the moment of crisis. He either was one in every ordinary moment before it, or he was not. About / Our Mission Declaration Pledge Lexicon Early Adopters How It Works Installation FAQs Contact & Support Counsel Handoff Events Noted Counsel Policies & Procedures Terms of Service Privacy Notice One fictional example • Five practical steps From a difficult moment to a record you can review. This walkthrough follows Alex, a fictional father documenting an exchange that did not take place. The example explains the intended workflow without claiming that a demonstration is a real case or proof of an event. Release clarity Steps describe the product workflow. Exact screens, supported file types, integrity checks, and export functions depend on the tested release. Actual release captures will be added after verification. 1. Capture what you personally observed Alex starts with the scheduled exchange date, the agreed place, and a short factual note about what happened. A useful entry separates the planned event from the observed result. It avoids guessing about another person's motives or turning a disagreement into a legal conclusion. The benefit is context while the details are fresh. Instead of returning weeks later to reconstruct a confusing afternoon, Alex has an identifiable event to review. If a detail is uncertain, the note should say so rather than invent precision. Use fictional records while learning the software. The website beta form is for contact and platform information, not for submitting the exchange details or the supporting evidence. 2. Keep supporting material and its source context Alex associates a harmless example message and receipt with the event. Source notes explain where each item came from and whether it is an original export, screenshot, or other copy. A screenshot can be useful without being equivalent to the underlying source record. Where supported by the release, file hashing creates a reference fingerprint for later comparison. It can help identify a change in file contents. It does not establish that Alex was at a location or that the account of the exchange is true. Original-file preservation, metadata retention, and custody logging must be verified before relying on a specific build. Keep independent source material and appropriate backups. 3. Connect the pieces in a chronology Alex connects the event with its supporting files and relevant order reference. The timeline gives the event a place among other dated records. That makes it easier to find the right material when preparing for a discussion. Organization is useful even when a record is incomplete. A missing attachment or uncertain date should remain visible as a gap. The software should not be presented as filling gaps with independently verified facts. The Windows workspace is the primary product. Mobile capture and Windows–Android synchronization are forthcoming work; this example does not depend on an announced synchronization feature. 4. Review the record before interpreting it Alex reads the event in sequence, checks the attached material, and corrects any inaccurate notes. Dates, source labels, names, and the distinction between observation and inference all matter. A repeated sequence can prompt a question without establishing a legal finding. The practical benefit is a clearer starting point for review. A lawyer can ask about a specific event and its source context instead of receiving an unexplained collection of images. P.O.P.S. does not replace that professional judgment. About / Our Mission Declaration Pledge Lexicon Early Adopters How It Works Installation FAQs Contact & Support Counsel Handoff Events Noted Counsel Policies & Procedures Terms of Service Privacy Notice First Order of Protection The Creed & The Pledge Preserve. Protect. Prove. The Creed The Charge I am the First Order of Protection. Before the law arrives, I am here. Before the danger is named, I am watching. Before my family asks, I have already decided: I will not fail them. I do not wait for permission to protect what is mine. I do not require a title to fulfill a calling. My badge is my presence. My oath was sworn the day I accepted this house as my charge. I will preserve what has been entrusted to me. I will protect those who cannot yet protect themselves. I will prove, by action, not by word, that the watchman did not sleep. Preserve Protect Prove This is not a slogan. This is the order of operations for every day I am given breath. The Pledge of Commitment I make this pledge not to an institution, but to the ones under my roof, and before the God who placed them in my care. Presence I pledge my presence: that I will be found, that I will be reachable, that I will not be a stranger in my own home. Vigilance I pledge my vigilance: that I will see the danger before it announces itself, and act before I am asked. Readiness I pledge my readiness: that whatever the moment requires, I will not be found unprepared, untrained, or unwilling. Record I pledge my record: that my actions will speak, and that if ever questioned, the proof of what I did and when I did it will stand on its own. Restraint I pledge my restraint: that my strength exists to shield, not to dominate; my authority exists to serve, not to rule. Permanence I pledge my permanence: that this charge does not end at the end of a shift, a season, or a hard year. It ends when I do, and not before. This is the First Order. This is Proof of Presence. From Philosophy to Practice Proof of Presence requires a record. The P.O.P.S. Pledge establishes the commitment. About / Our Mission Declaration Pledge Lexicon Early Adopters How It Works Installation FAQs Contact & Support Counsel Handoff Events Noted Counsel Policies & Procedures Terms of Service Privacy Notice Court Language Guide POPS Lexicon Plain-English courtroom terms, evidence language, and factual rewrite guidance for parents building disciplined records. Core Court Terms POPS helps users recognize courtroom language, understand it in plain English, and preserve facts in a clear, organized way. This guide is educational. It can help you understand terms you may encounter in court documents, hearings, attorney conversations, or case records. It does not replace legal advice or determine what should be filed in court. Rewrite guidance: Prefer facts over conclusions. Prefer dates, records, and actions over blame. Prefer documented events over legal labels. Search the POPS Lexicon Showing 10 of 10 terms · Court-safe explanations · Educational only All Terms High Sensitivity Evidence Court Procedure Constitutional Legal culpable High Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: Legally or morally responsible for wrongdoing. Why it matters: This word can sound like a legal conclusion, so POPS should encourage factual wording instead of blame. POPS use: Flag for attorney review if used in a report, packet, or filing. Court-safe example: The records show the scheduled parenting time did not occur on the dates listed. Open direct definition → Evidence exculpatory Medium Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: Evidence that may help show a person did not do something wrong or did comply with an order. Why it matters: Users should be able to tag records that may help show lawful conduct or a good-faith effort. POPS use: Allow tagging and evidence classification. Court-safe example: This message may be exculpatory because it shows I appeared at the exchange location on time. Open direct definition → Court Procedure pro se Medium Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: Representing yourself in court without an attorney. Why it matters: Many POPS users may be self-represented and need organizing help. POPS use: Show as informational and supportive, not as legal advice. Court-safe example: I am appearing pro se and have organized the attached records for the Court's review. Open direct definition → Legal Standard prima facie High Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: Something that appears sufficient on its face unless challenged by other evidence. Why it matters: This is a legal threshold term and should be used carefully. POPS use: Flag for review when used as a conclusion. Court-safe example: The timeline and records may show a prima facie pattern of missed parenting time. Open direct definition → Legal Doctrine estoppel High Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: A rule that may prevent someone from taking a position that conflicts with earlier words, actions, or promises when another person relied on them. Preserve the Truth. P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System is not a support group. It is a support machine. It was built for the father who is being denied access to his child and needs to move through the system with discipline, proof, and restraint. The Doctrine POPS is not a support group. It is a support machine. It was built for the father who is being denied access to his child and needs to move through the system with discipline, proof, and restraint. Not panic. Not revenge. Not desperation. A record. POPS exists because when a father's presence is questioned, emotion is not enough. Memory is not enough. Pain is not enough. The record has to stand. The Mission There is a place in a father that does not need to be taught. The instinct to protect. The duty to stand between harm and the child. The responsibility to show up, provide, guard, and remain accountable even when nobody is watching. That duty is not created by a court order. It is older than that. It lives in conscience, in blood, in faith, and in the charge placed inside a man to protect what has been entrusted to him. So when a father is separated from his child, that calling does not disappear. It becomes trapped. He is still a protector, but the door is locked. He is still responsible, but his hands are tied. He is still called a father, but treated like a visitor. He still carries the duty, but is denied the place to perform it. POPS was built for that place. Not to attack. Not to inflame. Not to spy. Not to turn pain into revenge. POPS exists to help a father preserve the truth when the truth is being contested. The Four Pillars Presence Presence is not just standing in a place. Presence is the call made, the message sent, the arrival at the exchange, the request for records, the follow-up after silence, and the lawful attempt when the door does not open. POPS is designed to help preserve a record of those attempts for later review. Protection Protection means guarding the child, the truth, the record, and the lawful path forward. Not aggression. Not intimidation. Not chaos. Discipline. Standing watch over the facts. Proof A painful story is not enough in court. A pattern needs structure. An event needs a date. A claim needs evidence. A file needs a hash. A timeline needs custody. A report needs restraint. POPS turns scattered facts into organized proof. Restraint Pain can make a person speak in ways that hurt their own case. POPS does not erase the pain. It preserves the original words, then helps translate the record into court-safe language. The truth stays strong without becoming reckless. How the System Thinks POPS follows a disciplined six-step product direction. The steps below describe intended behavior; extraction, sealing, custody logs, and report outputs require verification against the release supplied. The application organizes user-provided information and does not independently verify events. Capture Record what happened or upload a document, image, message export, receipt, court order, photo, screenshot, or other evidence. Preserve The original file is copied into protected local storage and hashed with SHA-256 so the system can later verify whether it changed. Extract When possible, POPS reads documents, images, screenshots, message exports, and court records to pull out dates, times, names, messages, case numbers, order language, and event detai

An organized record can make a discussion more focused: what happened, when it was recorded, and which material supports the account. P.O.P.S. is designed to help prepare that material while leaving professional judgment with counsel. Release clarity Attorney packet exports, selection controls, report formats, manifests, and verification artifacts require confirmation against the release supplied. This page is informational, not a live upload portal or a promise that every described output is available. Start with a defined scope In the fictional missed-exchange example, the user identifies the relevant time window and supporting records before sharing. The goal is to make the relationship between an event note, a source file, and an order reference understandable. It is not to send every private record automatically. Review the release's actual export controls before assuming that a date filter, selected-file bundle, or summary format exists. Users remain responsible for checking accuracy, completeness, relevance, and privacy. Intended packet contents, subject to validation Chronology and notes Selected dated events and factual descriptions, with uncertainty and user-supplied information identifiable. Evidence index and files A clear relationship between listed items and the selected supporting files. Original sources, copies, and annotations should be distinguishable. Manifest and integrity information A map of included artifacts and recorded hash values where supported. Exact formats and independent verification steps must be demonstrated. Source and handling context Available provenance and chain-of-custody information, with gaps or unverified details left explicit rather than silently assumed. Actual application screenshot pending A sanitized, actual generated packet with an index, a selected file, and any verified integrity report. This is an asset requirement, not a fabricated sample. This space is reserved for a verified capture of the release being offered. No application image has been fabricated. What the integrity information means SHA-256 creates a fingerprint from a file’s contents. Comparing a later fingerprint with a previously recorded value helps check whether those contents have changed. A match does not independently establish who created the file, when an event happened, or whether the information is true. Provenance records where material came from and how it was collected. Chain of custody documents its handling over time. A hash can support that history, but cannot replace it. Keep source material, record context accurately, and distinguish your own notes from system-recorded information. P.O.P.S. supports organization and review. It does not independently verify real-world events, provide legal advice, or guarantee that a file or report will be admitted in court. Review locally, then choose how to share Where export is supported, open the resulting package and check it before delivery. The website customer account does not store application evidence. Do not send a packet through a general beta, contact, or account form. A future counsel portal remains a roadmap direction, not a current upload or sharing service. The specific release and the user's chosen delivery method determine what can be shared.

About / Our Mission Declaration Pledge Lexicon Early Adopters How It Works Installation FAQs Contact & Support Counsel Handoff Events Noted Counsel Policies & Procedures Terms of Service Privacy Notice POPS GOVERNANCE Policies and Procedures Clear operating standards for Proof of Presence System, Open Door Access, evidence organization, and POPS Noted Counsel. 1. Purpose and Operating Doctrine P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System - helps parents organize facts, preserve records, document good-faith effort, and prepare clearer materials for attorney or court review. POPS is not a law firm. POPS does not provide legal advice, legal representation, legal strategy, or a guarantee of any court result, attorney acceptance, evidence admissibility, or case outcome. 1.1 Core Principle Turn emotion into facts. Turn facts into organized proof. Turn proof into a clearer case file. 1.2 Product Boundary POPS is built to help a parent document what happened, identify the supporting record, organize chronology, and prepare materials for review. It is not built to attack another parent, create revenge material, spy on anyone, or tell a user what legal action to take. 2. Acceptable Use Policy Users must use POPS lawfully, honestly, and with respect for the privacy and rights of others. 2.1 Prohibited Uses Creating, altering, fabricating, or misrepresenting evidence Using POPS to stalk, intimidate, threaten, harass, or retaliate Accessing another person's device, account, or private records without permission Uploading or sharing private information through unapproved channels Using POPS as a substitute for emergency services or qualified legal counsel Presenting POPS-generated material as legal advice, a court order, or verified fact without review 3. Evidence and Record Integrity Procedure POPS helps users organize records. The user remains responsible for the accuracy, completeness, source, and lawful possession of every record they enter, attach, export, or share. 3.1 Preserve Originals Where Possible Users should preserve original messages, native exports, documents, photos, receipts, call logs, and other source material where possible. Screenshots may be useful reference copies, but they can lack source metadata and should not be treated as automatically equivalent to an original record. 3.2 Factual Entry Standard Incident, communication, timeline, and evidence entries should state what occurred, when it occurred, who was involved, what supporting record exists, and what the user personally did. Users should avoid insults, speculation, unsupported accusations, and emotional conclusions. 3.3 User Review Before Export Before exporting or sharing a report, packet, timeline, or statement, the user must review it for accuracy, privacy, completeness, and relevance. POPS does not independently verify the truth of a user's records. 4. Privacy and Operational Boundary POPS is designed around a local-first principle: a parent's family records should remain under that parent's control unless they deliberately choose to export, share, upload, or submit something through a feature that clearly states it will transmit information. 4.1 Do Not Send Private Case Evidence Through General Forms General POPS contact, support, Open Door, and Noted Counsel forms are not for court orders, child names, medical records, school records, screenshots, private messages, audio, video, passwords, Social Security numbers, financial information, or evidence files unless POPS specifically provides a secure purpose-built upload process. 4.2 User Device Responsibility Users are responsible for se

Privacy Principle POPS is designed around a local-first principle: family records should remain under the user's control unless the user deliberately chooses to export, share, upload, submit, or transmit them. The POPS website and the POPS desktop application serve different functions. The website is a public information, support, and access channel. The desktop application is intended to help users organize their own case records locally. POPS does not promise automatic cloud backup, encrypted storage, attorney sharing, permanent evidence preservation, or remote access unless a specific active product feature clearly states that it is enabled and explains how it works. 2. Information POPS May Receive POPS may receive information that a person voluntarily enters through a website form, purchase process, account process, support request, Open Door Access request, or Noted Counsel submission. 2.1 Information You May Provide Name, email address, and contact message Purchase, license, or access-request information Support questions and product-feedback information Open Door Access information necessary to review an access request Noted Counsel Merit Recognition information submitted for review 2.2 Basic Technical Information Website hosting, security, email, payment, and analytics providers may process limited technical information needed to deliver the website, prevent abuse, maintain security, diagnose technical problems, or measure basic site performance. This may include information such as browser type, device type, IP address, page request information, timestamps, and referral source. POPS does not use this information to build profiles about a user's private family case, child, court matter, medical situation, or legal dispute. 3. Information POPS Does Not Request Through General Forms Do not send private case evidence through a general POPS contact form, social-media message, ordinary support email, Open Door request, or Noted Counsel submission. Unless POPS provides a clearly identified secure process, do not send: Child names, birth dates, addresses, or school identifiers Case numbers, court orders, pleadings, or attorney work product Medical records, school records, or therapy information Private texts, emails, screenshots, audio, video, or evidence files Passwords, account credentials, Social Security numbers, or bank information Emergency information or information requiring immediate legal action POPS may delete, redact, decline to process, or request removal of sensitive information submitted through an inappropriate channel. 4. Local Application Records POPS is intended to help users organize timelines, communications, evidence references, incident notes, court-order details, and reports on their own device. Users remain responsible for protecting their device, operating-system account, passwords, exported files, backups, and any information they choose to share with an attorney, court, advocate, family member, cloud provider, or another person. 4.1 Export Is a User Decision When POPS provides an export or report feature, the user decides what to export and where to send it. Know what is available, what remains under validation, and what a website account or saved cart actually means. What is P.O.P.S.? P.O.P.S. means Proof of Presence System. It is installable Windows software designed primarily for fathers documenting parenting-time experiences. Its purpose is to bring event notes, supporting files, case context, and chronology together for personal review and discussions with counsel. The website is the product and customer-access surface; it is not your private Evidence Vault. Is there a mandatory subscription? The standard Windows license follows a one-time purchase model without a mandatory recurring subscription. The existing published Guardian price is $99. Optional annual maintenance is listed at $19.99, but its precise coverage and launch availability require confirmation. No new recurring plan, automatic renewal, or lifetime upgrade entitlement is promised here. Checkout is currently unavailable. What does Guardian Access include? The published offer describes a Windows desktop license with lifetime P.O.P.S. Membership included. Feature availability depends on the release supplied. Supported Windows versions, device limits, update rights, installation requirements, delivery timing, and refund terms must be finalized before purchases open. Android access is not promised as part of this license. How is beta participation different from buying? Beta enrollment expresses interest in testing and providing feedback. A saved application is not an invitation, a paid license, or a guaranteed place. The program aims for 50 active participants. Participation terms and any access arrangements will be supplied with an invitation. Purchasing does not automatically enroll you in testing. What is the first-100 customer program? The founding-customer presentation is intended for the first 100 qualifying paying customers. Special benefits and qualification rules are not yet approved. There is no discount or additional entitlement to claim today. A cart item or account registration does not establish first-100 status; that would require verified qualifying completed purchases. Is Android available? The Android companion is being prepared. Intended mobile capture, photo and location provenance, offline-first work, and synchronization with Windows are under development or validation. No download date, device compatibility list, transfer method, or Android license entitlement is promised. See the Android page for the current distinction between intended and available functions. Does a hash prove that an event happened? No. SHA-256 can help compare file contents with a recorded reference. It does not establish that an event occurred, that a statement is accurate, or that a location or timestamp is independently verified. Provenance and handling context are separate records. Users remain responsible for accuracy and lawful collection. Can I export an attorney-ready packet? Structured timelines, selected files, indexes, manifests, and integrity reports are intended handoff outputs. Exact formats and contents require verification against the release being supplied. Do not assume every listed output is available. Counsel decides what is useful for a matter; P.O.P.S. does not guarantee legal acceptance or admissibility.
